title: Food Chains and Food Webs
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Food Chains and Food Webs Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Energy is needed for life: producers, consumers and decomposers, energy pyramids, food chains (grass to rabbit to lynx) and food webs. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 3, Biology)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets (BC): producers, consumers and decomposers, food chains, food webs and energy from the Sun. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy flows from the Sun to producers to consumers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants are producers: they use sunlight to make their own food. Animals are consumers: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both. Decomposers such as bacteria, fungi and worms break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil.

A food chain shows who eats whom: grass → rabbit → lynx. The arrow points from the food to the eater. Food chains that link together make a food web. Less energy is left at each step, so there are fewer top predators.

Example

In grass → hare → lynx, which is the producer?

Producers make their own food.

Answer: grass

Example

What do decomposers do?

Think of a fallen log.

Answer: break down dead things and return nutrients

Common mistakes

  • Drawing the arrow from the eater to the food.
  • Thinking the Sun is a producer.
  • Forgetting decomposers.

faq.q: Why are there fewer wolves than rabbits?
faq.a: Each step up a food chain has less energy, so it can feed fewer animals.

faq.q: What happens if one animal in a food web disappears?
faq.a: Its predators lose food and its prey may increase.

items.q: Is saltbush a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Producers make their own food from sunlight.

items.q: Food chain: phytoplankton → krill → whale. What eats the krill in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Food chain: grain → field vole → kestrel. What eats the field vole in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Are phytoplankton producers, consumers or decomposers?
items.e: Producers make their own food from sunlight.

items.q: Food chain: dandelion → snail → song thrush → cat. What does the song thrush eat in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: In the same forest web, a disease kills most of the oak trees. Which animals lose food first?
items.e: Herbivores depend directly on the producer.

items.q: Which living things are consumers?
c: animals, because they eat other living things
items.e: Consumers cannot make their own food.

items.q: Food chain: acorns → wood mouse → tawny owl. Which is the first consumer (it eats the producer)?
items.e: It eats the plant at the start of the chain.

items.q: What does a producer need to make its food?
c: sunlight, water and carbon dioxide from the air
items.e: Plants make food in their leaves.

items.q: What is prey?
c: an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal
items.e: Mice are prey for owls.

items.q: Are bacteria in the soil producers, consumers or decomposers?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: Is a dung beetle a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: Why are decomposers important?
c: They break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil for plants.
items.e: Without them, dead matter would pile up.

items.q: Food chain: oak leaves → caterpillar → blue tit → sparrowhawk. What does the blue tit eat in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: What would happen if there were no decomposers?
c: Dead plants and animals would pile up and soil would lose nutrients.
items.e: Decomposers recycle nutrients.

items.q: Food chain: pondweed → tadpole → water beetle → heron. Which is the top predator?
items.e: The top predator is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

items.q: Food chain: grain → field vole → kestrel. Which is the producer?
items.e: The producer makes its own food using sunlight; it is always first.

items.q: Which is a herbivore?
items.e: Moose eat plants only.

items.q: Food chain: nettles → aphid → ladybug → blackbird. Which is the top predator?
items.e: The top predator is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

items.q: Meadow food chain: clover → grasshopper → garter snake → red-tailed hawk. Which is a carnivore that is also eaten?
items.e: The snake eats grasshoppers and is eaten by hawks.

items.q: This is a meadow food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: grass → grasshopper → mouse → fox.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: acorns, tawny owl, wood mouse?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Pond food web: algae and duckweed are eaten by tadpoles and snails. Fish eat tadpoles. Herons eat fish and frogs. Which living things are producers?
items.e: Producers are the plants and algae.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that eats only animals?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: field vole, grain, kestrel?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: cat, dandelion, snail, song thrush?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a predator?
c: a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
a living thing that eats only plants
a living thing that eats only animals
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a prey?
c: a living thing that is hunted and eaten by other animals
a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
a living thing that eats only animals
a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: krill, phytoplankton, whale?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that is hunted and eaten by other animals?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Use the coral reef food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
c: phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → squid → shark
shark → phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → squid
phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → squid → parrotfish
shark → squid → small fish → zooplankton → phytoplankton
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → squid → shark.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that makes its own food using energy from sunlight?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a producer?
c: a living thing that makes its own food using energy from sunlight
a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
a living thing that eats only animals
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Look at the ocean food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: phytoplankton → krill → humpback whale.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: algae, mayfly larva, otter, trout?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that hunts and eats other animals?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: What does an arrow in a food chain show?
c: the direction energy moves when one thing is eaten
items.e: The arrow points to the eater.

items.q: In a pond: algae → tadpole → fish → heron. Which is the top consumer?
items.e: The heron is at the end of the chain.

items.q: Where does the energy in almost every food chain come from first?
items.e: Plants use the Sun's energy to make food.

items.q: Use the school garden food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: grass → grasshopper → mynah → snake.

items.q: This is a school garden food web. How many kinds of food does the caterpillar eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the caterpillar: hibiscus.

items.q: Use the pond food web. In this web, the dragonfly nymph's food is: mosquito larva. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only animals.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. In this web, the dragonfly nymph's food is: mosquito larva. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only animals.

items.q: Use the coral reef food web. What does the small fish eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the zooplankton to the small fish, so the small fish eats zooplankton.

items.q: Look at the forest food web. Which animal eats the oak tree?
items.e: An arrow goes from the oak tree to the caterpillar.

items.q: Look at the school garden food web. Which of these is food for the snake?
items.e: The arrow goes from the mynah to the snake, so the snake eats a mynah.

items.q: What is a food web?
c: many food chains that are linked together
items.e: Most animals eat more than one thing.

items.q: A wolf eats deer. A deer eats grass. What is the deer?
items.e: Deer eat only plants.

items.q: Lake food chain: algae → zooplankton → minnow → walleye. What does the minnow eat?
items.e: Follow the arrow into the minnow.

items.q: This is a meadow food web. Which animal eats the wildflowers?
items.e: An arrow goes from the wildflowers to the mouse.

items.q: This is a meadow food web. How many kinds of food does the snake eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the snake: mouse, frog.

items.q: This is a meadow food web. Which of these is food for the fox?
items.e: The arrow goes from the mouse to the fox, so the fox eats a mouse.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. In this web, the turtle's food is: snail, water lettuce. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats both plants and animals.

items.q: Use the pond food web. Which animal eats the pondweed?
items.e: An arrow goes from the pondweed to the turtle.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. How many kinds of food does the snake eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the snake: mouse, frog.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. Which of these is food for the heron?
items.e: The arrow goes from the guppy to the heron, so the heron eats a guppy.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. In this web, the small fish's food is: mosquito larva, algae. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats both plants and animals.

items.q: This is a coral reef food web. Which animal eats the seaweed?
items.e: An arrow goes from the seaweed to the sea urchin.

items.q: This is a forest food web. What does the squirrel eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the oak tree to the squirrel, so the squirrel eats an oak tree.

items.q: Use the coral reef food web. Which animal eats the squid?
items.e: An arrow goes from the squid to the shark.

items.q: Look at the school garden food web. A disease kills most of the aphids. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The ladybug eats only aphids. Without them, the ladybug has little food.

items.q: What do decomposers return to the soil?
items.e: Nutrients help new plants grow.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. Most of the snakes are removed from the meadow. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the snake eats frogs. With fewer predators, more frogs survive.

items.q: This is a pond food web. Most of the frogs are removed from the pond. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the frog eats dragonfly nymphs. With fewer predators, more dragonfly nymphs survive.

items.q: Look at the forest food web. A disease kills most of the oak trees. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The caterpillar eats only oak trees. Without them, the caterpillar has little food.

items.q: Food chain: algae → mayfly larva → trout → otter. If the number of mayfly larvae fell, what would most likely happen to the trout?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Use the ocean food web. Most of the orcas are removed from the ocean. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the orca eats seals. With fewer predators, more seals survive.

items.q: Forest food web: acorns are eaten by squirrels, chipmunks and deer. Foxes eat squirrels and chipmunks. Wolves eat deer. What does the fox eat?
items.e: Read the links to the fox.

items.q: Food chain: seaweed → periwinkle → crab → herring gull. If the number of periwinkles fell, what would most likely happen to the crabs?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Food chain: pondweed → tadpole → water beetle → heron. If all the tadpoles were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer pondweed.
There would probably be more pondweed.
items.e: With no tadpoles eating them, more pondweed survive.

items.q: Which living thing is a decomposer?
items.e: Fungi break down dead things.

items.q: This is a meadow food web. A disease kills most of the grass. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The grasshopper eats only grass. Without them, the grasshopper has little food.

items.q: A farmer sprays a field to kill all the grasshoppers. What might happen to the frogs that eat them?
c: The frogs have less food and their number may fall.
items.e: Changes travel through food webs.

items.q: Food chain: acorns → wood mouse → tawny owl. If all the tawny owls were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be more wood mice.
There would probably be fewer wood mice.
items.e: With no tawny owls eating them, more wood mice survive.

items.q: Food chain: grass → rabbit → fox. If the number of rabbits fell, what would most likely happen to the foxes?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: This is a pond food web. A disease kills most of the mosquito larvae. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The dragonfly nymph eats only mosquito larvae. Without them, the dragonfly nymph has little food.

items.q: Food chain: algae → mayfly larva → trout → otter. If all the otters were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer trout.
There would probably be more trout.
items.e: With no otters eating them, more trout survive.

items.q: Food chain: dandelion → snail → song thrush → cat. If the number of snails fell, what would most likely happen to the song thrushes?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: This is a school garden food web. A disease kills most of the hibiscus plants. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The aphid eats only hibiscus plants. Without them, the aphid has little food.

items.q: Which animal is an omnivore?
c: a black bear (eats berries and fish)
items.e: Omnivores eat plants and animals.

items.q: What is a food web?
c: a web made by a spider
many food chains in one ecosystem that connect
items.e: A food web shows how many food chains overlap, because most animals eat more than one thing.

items.q: Use the pond food web. The energy in the frog's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the frog.

items.q: A carnivore eats
items.e: Hawks and wolves are carnivores.

items.q: What does a food chain show?
c: what eats what, and how energy passes from one living thing to another
items.e: Arrows show energy flow.

items.q: A herbivore eats
items.e: Rabbits and deer are herbivores.

items.q: Which organisms break down dead plants and animals?
c: decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria
items.e: Decomposers return matter from dead organisms to the soil.

items.q: What is prey?
c: an animal that is hunted and eaten
items.e: Rabbits are prey for foxes.

items.q: This is a forest food web. The energy in the owl's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the owl.

items.q: Use the pond food web. The energy in the dragonfly nymph's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the dragonfly nymph.

items.q: In a food chain, what does an arrow show?
c: that the first organism eats the second
the direction food energy and matter move, from the food to the eater
items.e: An arrow from grass to rabbit means the rabbit eats the grass; matter and energy move to the rabbit.

items.q: Which change would affect the most organisms in a food web?
items.e: Every food chain begins with producers, so all consumers depend on them.

items.q: Farmers released ladybugs into a vegetable farm with many aphids. What is the most likely result?
items.e: Ladybugs are predators of aphids.

items.q: Which is a scavenger that eats dead animals?
items.e: Scavengers clean up dead animals.

items.q: Every food chain starts with
items.e: Producers make the food that all the other organisms depend on.

items.q: What is a top predator?
c: the first living thing in a chain
an animal at the end of a food chain that nothing in the chain eats
items.e: Such as an owl or a fox.

items.q: An omnivore eats
items.e: Bears and many birds are omnivores.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. The energy in the guppy's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the guppy.

items.q: What is a consumer?
c: a plant that makes its own food
an organism that gets energy by eating other organisms
items.e: Animals are consumers. They cannot make their own food.

items.q: A graph shows that when the number of snakes in a garden fell, the number of mynahs rose. What is the best explanation?
c: Fewer mynahs were eaten by snakes.
items.e: Fewer predators means more prey survive.

items.q: Ava says the arrow in “grass → rabbit” means the grass eats the rabbit. How should she read it?
c: The arrow shows the rabbit is bigger.
The arrow shows the rabbit eats the grass (matter moves to the rabbit).
The arrow shows the rabbit lives in grass.
items.e: Arrows point to the eater, in the direction matter and energy move.
